27:1: Interpretation of Surat An-Naml It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed the separate letters at the beginning of the surahs in Surah Al-Baqarah. And the Almighty’s saying: These are verses meaning these are verses of the Qur’an and a clear Book meaning clear and plain a guidance and good tidings for the believers meaning that guidance and good tidings from the Qur’an are only attained by those who believe in it, follow it, and confirm it, and act in accordance with what is in it, and establish the prescribed prayers, and pay the obligatory zakat, and are certain of the Hereafter, and the resurrection after death, and the reward for deeds: good and evil, and Paradise and Hell, as God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guidance and healing. But as for those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness’” (Al-Baqarah 2:17). And God the Almighty said: That you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a quarrelsome people. That is why God the Almighty said here: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter meaning, they deny it and rule out its occurrence We have made their deeds pleasing to them, so they wander blindly meaning, what they are in has been made beautiful to them, and We have extended their error, so they wander in their misguidance. This was a recompense for what they denied of the Hereafter, as God the Almighty said: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time 13:1. Those are the ones for whom is the worst punishment meaning, in this world and the Hereafter, and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers meaning, no one among the people of the gathering will lose themselves and their wealth except them. And the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, you receive the Qur’an from One Who is Wise and Knowing. That is, And indeed, you, O Muhammad - Qatada said: you receive means you take the Qur’an from One Who is Wise and Knowing. That is, from One Who is Wise and Knowing, that is, Wise in His commands and prohibitions, Knowing of all matters: great and small. So His report is pure truth, and His judgment is complete justice, as the Almighty said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice.

27:7: God Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminding him of what happened with Moses, peace be upon him, how God chose him and spoke to him and spoke to him privately, gave him great and dazzling signs and compelling evidence, and sent him to Pharaoh and his people, but they denied them and disbelieved and were too arrogant to follow him and submit to him. So God Almighty says: When Moses said to his family, meaning remember when Moses was walking with his family and lost his way, and that was at night and in the darkness, and he perceived a fire on the side of the mountain, meaning he saw a fire blazing and blazing, so he said, “To his family, ‘Indeed, I have perceived a fire. I will bring you information from it,’” meaning about the road, or I will bring you a burning flame that you may warm yourselves, meaning that you may warm yourself from it. And it was as he said. So he returned from it with great report, and took from it a great light, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And when he came to it, he was called, ‘Blessed are those in the Fire and those around it.’ That is, when he came to it and saw a tremendous and amazing sight where he reached it, and the fire was blazing in a green tree, the fire only increasing in intensity, and the tree only increasing in greenness and freshness. Then he raised his head, and behold, its light was connected to the reins of the sky. Ibn Abbas and others said: It was not fire, but rather a glowing light. In a narration from Ibn Abbas: The light of the Lord of the worlds. So Moses stood amazed at what he saw: It was called, ‘Blessed are those in the Fire.’ Ibn Abbas said: Hallowed be He, ‘and those around it,’ meaning the angels. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib narrated to us, Abu Dawud - he is al-Tayalisi - narrated to us, Shu'bah and al-Mas'udi narrated to us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, who heard Abu Ubaidah narrating on the authority of Abu Musa may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "God does not sleep, nor is it befitting for Him to sleep. He lowers the balance and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before those of the day, and the deeds of the day before those of the night." Al-Mas'udi added: "And His veil is either light or fire. Were He to remove it, the radiance of His face would burn up everything that His sight encompasses." Then Abu Ubaidah recited: Blessed is he who is in the Fire and he who is around it. The original hadith is narrated in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah. God the Almighty says: And exalted is God, Lord of the worlds, who does what He wills, and nothing of His creation resembles Him, and nothing of His making encompasses Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great, distinct from all creation, and the earth and the heavens do not encompass Him. Rather, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge, free from resemblance to created things. And the saying of God the Almighty: O Moses, indeed I am God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise He informed him that the One who was addressing him and conversing with him was his Lord, God the Exalted in Might, Who has subdued and overcome all things, the Wise in His words and deeds. Then He ordered him to throw down his staff from his hand to show him clear evidence that He is the Doer, the Chosen One, and the Able to do all things. So when Moses threw that staff from his hand, it immediately turned into a huge, terrifying snake, extremely large and yet moving quickly. That is why God the Almighty said: But when he saw it writhing as if it were a jinn The jinn are a type of snake that are the fastest moving and most agitated. In the hadith, it is forbidden to kill the jinn of houses. So when Moses saw that, he turned back and did not look back meaning he did not turn around out of extreme fear. "O Moses, do not fear. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear" meaning do not fear what you see, for I want to choose you as a Messenger and make you a distinguished prophet. And the saying of God the Almighty: Except for he who has wronged and then substituted evil for good, then indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. This is an isolated exception and in it is great glad tidings for mankind, for whoever was doing a bad deed and then desisted from it, returned, repented and turned back, then God will accept his repentance, as God the Almighty said: And indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance. And the Almighty said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself (Al-An’am 2:17), and there are many verses on this subject. And the saying of God the Almighty: And put your hand into the bosom of your garment; it will come out white without disease. This is another verse and a dazzling proof of the power of God, the Doer of Choice, and the truthfulness of those who attributed a miracle to Him. God the Almighty commanded him to put his hand into the bosom of his armor, and when he put it in and took it out, it would come out white and radiant, like a piece of the moon with a shine that glittered like a flash of lightning. And the Almighty’s saying: In nine signs meaning these are two of nine signs with which I support you and make them proof for you to Pharaoh and his people Indeed, they were a wicked people. And these are the nine signs of which God Almighty said: And We gave Moses nine clear signs, as was previously explained there. And the Almighty said: So when Our clear signs came to them, meaning clear, evident, they said, ‘This is obvious magic,’ and they wanted to oppose it with their magic, but they were defeated and turned back humiliated. And they denied it, in the outward appearance of their matter, while their souls were convinced of it, meaning they knew in their souls that it was the truth from God, but they denied it, were stubborn about it, and were arrogant toward it. Out of injustice and haughtiness, meaning out of injustice from their souls, a cursed trait, and out of arrogance, meaning, arrogance from following the truth. For this reason, the Almighty said: Then see how was the end of the corrupters, meaning, look, O Muhammad, how was the end of their matter in God’s destruction of them and drowning them all in a single morning. The gist of the address is: Beware, you who deny Muhammad and deny what he brought from his Lord, that what happened to them will happen to you by way of foremost and most appropriate, for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more noble and greater than Moses, and his proof is more convincing and stronger than Moses’ proof with the evidence that God gave him. Associated with his existence in himself and his characteristics, and the glad tidings that preceded him from the prophets about him, and the covenants that were taken for him, upon him be the best prayers and peace from his Lord.

Then Abu Ubaidah recited: Blessed is he who is in the Fire and he who is around it. The original hadith is narrated in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah. God the Almighty says: And exalted is God, Lord of the worlds, who does what He wills, and nothing of His creation resembles Him, and nothing of His making encompasses Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great, distinct from all creation, and the earth and the heavens do not encompass Him. Rather, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge, free from resemblance to created things. And the saying of God the Almighty: O Moses, indeed I am God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise He informed him that the One who was addressing him and conversing with him was his Lord, God the Exalted in Might, Who has subdued and overcome all things, the Wise in His words and deeds. Then He ordered him to throw down his staff from his hand to show him clear evidence that He is the Doer, the Chosen One, and the Able to do all things. So when Moses threw that staff from his hand, it immediately turned into a huge, terrifying snake, extremely large and yet moving quickly. That is why God the Almighty said: But when he saw it writhing as if it were a jinn The jinn are a type of snake that are the fastest moving and most agitated. In the hadith, it is forbidden to kill the jinn of houses. So when Moses saw that, he turned back and did not look back meaning he did not turn around out of extreme fear. "O Moses, do not fear. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear" meaning do not fear what you see, for I want to choose you as a Messenger and make you a distinguished prophet. And the saying of God the Almighty: Except for he who has wronged and then substituted evil for good, then indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. This is an isolated exception and in it is great glad tidings for mankind, for whoever was doing a bad deed and then desisted from it, returned, repented and turned back, then God will accept his repentance, as God the Almighty said: And indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance. And the Almighty said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself (Al-An’am 2:17), and there are many verses on this subject. And the saying of God the Almighty: And put your hand into the bosom of your garment; it will come out white without disease. This is another verse and a dazzling proof of the power of God, the Doer of Choice, and the truthfulness of those who attributed a miracle to Him. God the Almighty commanded him to put his hand into the bosom of his armor, and when he put it in and took it out, it would come out white and radiant, like a piece of the moon with a shine that glittered like a flash of lightning. And the Almighty’s saying: In nine signs meaning these are two of nine signs with which I support you and make them proof for you to Pharaoh and his people Indeed, they were a wicked people. And these are the nine signs of which God Almighty said: And We gave Moses nine clear signs, as was previously explained there. And the Almighty said: So when Our clear signs came to them, meaning clear, evident, they said, ‘This is obvious magic,’ and they wanted to oppose it with their magic, but they were defeated and turned back humiliated. And they denied it, in the outward appearance of their matter, while their souls were convinced of it, meaning they knew in their souls that it was the truth from God, but they denied it, were stubborn about it, and were arrogant toward it. Out of injustice and haughtiness, meaning out of injustice from their souls, a cursed trait, and out of arrogance, meaning, arrogance from following the truth. For this reason, the Almighty said: Then see how was the end of the corrupters, meaning, look, O Muhammad, how was the end of their matter in God’s destruction of them and drowning them all in a single morning. The gist of the address is: Beware, you who deny Muhammad and deny what he brought from his Lord, that what happened to them will happen to you by way of foremost and most appropriate, for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more noble and greater than Moses, and his proof is more convincing and stronger than Moses’ proof with the evidence that God gave him. Associated with his existence in himself and his characteristics, and the glad tidings that preceded him from the prophets about him, and the covenants that were taken for him, upon him be the best prayers and peace from his Lord.
27:15: God the Almighty tells us about the abundant blessings, sublime gifts, and beautiful attributes He bestowed upon His servants and prophets: David and his son Solomon, peace be upon them, and what He combined for them between the happiness of this world and the hereafter, and the kingdom and complete empowerment in this world, and the prophethood and message in religion. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, 'Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.' Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Tamam, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather, who said: Omar bin Abdul Aziz wrote: God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant for whom he praises God, except that his praise is better than his blessing. If only you could have known that from the revealed Book of God. God the Almighty said: And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, 'Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.' So what blessing is better than what was given to David and Solomon, peace be upon them. And the Almighty’s saying: And Solomon inherited David means in the kingdom and prophethood. What is meant is not the inheritance of wealth, because if that were the case, Solomon would not have been singled out from among the rest of David’s sons, as David had one hundred wives. Rather, what is meant by that is the inheritance of the kingdom and prophethood, because the wealth of the prophets is not inherited, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us in his saying: “We, the company of prophets, are not inherited. What we leave behind is charity.” And he said: O people, we have been taught the language of birds and have been given of all things, meaning, he informed Solomon of God’s blessings upon him in what He bestowed upon him of complete kingdom and great empowerment, to the point that He subjected to him mankind, jinn and birds, and he also knew the language of birds and animals. This is something that no human being was given, according to what we know of what God and His Messenger informed us of. And whoever among the ignorant and common folk claims that animals spoke like the speech of the sons of Adam before Solomon, son of David, as many people may utter, then this is a statement without knowledge. And if that were the case, then singling Solomon out would have been of no benefit, because all of them hear the speech of birds and animals, and know what She says, "It is not as they claimed or said. Rather, the animals, birds, and all other creatures have been in this form and manner since they were created until our time. But God Almighty had made Solomon understand what the birds communicate with in the air, and what the animals of different kinds speak. That is why God Almighty said: 'We have been taught the language of birds, and we have been given of all things,' meaning of what the king needs. 'Indeed, this is the manifest bounty,' meaning the apparent and clear bounty of God upon us." Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr, on the authority of al-Muttalib, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “David, peace be upon him, was extremely jealous. Whenever he went out, the doors would be closed, and no one would enter upon his family until he returned.” He said: “One day he went out and the doors were closed. A woman came looking into the house and saw a man standing in the middle of the house. She said to those in the house: ‘How did this man enter when the house is closed? By God, we will disgrace David.’ So David, peace be upon him, came and saw the man standing in the middle of the house. David said to him: ‘Who are you?’ He said: ‘He who does not fear kings and does not refrain from being veiled.’ David said: ‘Then you are, by God, the Angel of Death, welcoming the command of God.’ David curled up in his place until his soul was taken, until he had finished his business and the sun rose upon him. So Solomon, peace be upon him, said to the birds: ‘Shade David.’ So the birds shaded him until the earth became dark. So Solomon said to them: ‘Breath one wing at a time.’” Abu Hurayrah said: “O The Messenger of God, how did the birds do? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew his hand and the Madhrahiyyah overcame him that day. Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: The Madhrahiyyah are the red vultures. God the Almighty said: “And there were gathered before Solomon his soldiers of jinn and men and birds, and they were in ranks.” That is, He gathered before Solomon his soldiers of jinn, men and birds, meaning he rode among them with great grandeur and majesty. The humans were the ones who followed him, and the jinn were after them in status, and the birds had a status above his head. If he was hot, they shaded him from it with their wings. His statement: and they were in ranks means that the first of them would hold back the last of them so that no one would advance beyond the status that was set for him. Mujahid said: He made a division for each group, returning the first of them to the last of them so that they would not advance in the march as kings do today. And His saying: Until, when they came upon the Valley of the Ants, meaning, when Solomon, peace be upon him, passed with the armies and soldiers who were with him, by the Valley of the Ants, An ant said, ‘O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not.’ Ibn Asakir reported, through Ishaq bin Bishr, from Saeed, from Qatada, from Al-Hasan, that the name of this ant was Haras, and that it was from a tribe called Banu Al-Shisaan, and that it was lame and was the size of a wolf, meaning it feared that the horses would crush it with their hooves, so it ordered them to enter their dwellings, and Solomon, peace be upon him, understood that from it. Then he smiled, laughing at her words, and said, ‘My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve.’ Meaning, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me, such as teaching me the language of birds and animals. And upon my father to submit to You and believe in You, and to do righteousness that pleases You, meaning work that You love and are pleased with, and admit me by Your mercy into Your righteous servants, meaning if You take my life, then include me with the righteous among Your servants and the highest companion of Your friends. And whoever among the commentators said that this valley was in the land of Ash-Sham or elsewhere, and that this ant had two wings like a fly or other such sayings, then there is no basis for them. On the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali, who said: The ants of Solomon were like wolves. This is how I saw it, marked with the double ya’ from below, but it is with the unified ba’, and that is a typo, and God knows best. The point is that Solomon, peace be upon him, understood her words and smiled, laughing at that, and this is a very serious matter. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Abu Al-Siddiq Al-Naji, who said: Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both, went out to pray for rain, and there he saw an ant lying on its back, raising its legs to the sky and saying: O God, we are one of Your creations, and we cannot do without Your rain, and if You do not rain on us, we will perish. Solomon said: Go back, for you have been watered by the supplication of someone other than yourselves. It was proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “An ant bit one of the prophets, so he ordered the ant colony to be burned. Then God revealed to him: ‘Because an ant bit you, did you destroy a nation of nations that glorify God? Why not just one ant?’”

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr, on the authority of al-Muttalib, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “David, peace be upon him, was extremely jealous. Whenever he went out, the doors would be closed, and no one would enter upon his family until he returned.” He said: “One day he went out and the doors were closed. A woman came looking into the house and saw a man standing in the middle of the house. She said to those in the house: ‘How did this man enter when the house is closed? By God, we will disgrace David.’ So David, peace be upon him, came and saw the man standing in the middle of the house. David said to him: ‘Who are you?’ He said: ‘He who does not fear kings and does not refrain from being veiled.’ David said: ‘Then you are, by God, the Angel of Death, welcoming the command of God.’ David curled up in his place until his soul was taken, until he had finished his business and the sun rose upon him. So Solomon, peace be upon him, said to the birds: ‘Shade David.’ So the birds shaded him until the earth became dark. So Solomon said to them: ‘Breath one wing at a time.’” Abu Hurayrah said: “O The Messenger of God, how did the birds do? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew his hand and the Madhrahiyyah overcame him that day. Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: The Madhrahiyyah are the red vultures. God the Almighty said: “And there were gathered before Solomon his soldiers of jinn and men and birds, and they were in ranks.” That is, He gathered before Solomon his soldiers of jinn, men and birds, meaning he rode among them with great grandeur and majesty. The humans were the ones who followed him, and the jinn were after them in status, and the birds had a status above his head. If he was hot, they shaded him from it with their wings. His statement: and they were in ranks means that the first of them would hold back the last of them so that no one would advance beyond the status that was set for him. Mujahid said: He made a division for each group, returning the first of them to the last of them so that they would not advance in the march as kings do today. And His saying: Until, when they came upon the Valley of the Ants, meaning, when Solomon, peace be upon him, passed with the armies and soldiers who were with him, by the Valley of the Ants, An ant said, ‘O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you while they perceive not.’ Ibn Asakir reported on the authority of Ishaq bin Bishr on the authority of Saeed on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Al-Hasan that the name of this ant was Haras, and that it was from a tribe called Banu Al-Shisaan, and that it was lame and was the size of a wolf, meaning it feared that the horses would crush it with their hooves, so it ordered them to enter their dwellings, and Solomon, peace be upon him, understood that from it. Then he smiled, laughing at her words, and said, ‘My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve.’ Meaning, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me by teaching me the language of birds and animals. And upon my father to submit to You and believe in You, and to do righteousness that pleases You, meaning work that You love and are pleased with, and admit me by Your mercy into Your righteous servants, meaning if You take my life, then include me with the righteous among Your servants and the highest companion of Your friends. And whoever among the commentators said that this valley was in the land of Ash-Sham or elsewhere, and that this ant had two wings like a fly or other such sayings, then there is no basis for them. On the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali, who said: The ants of Solomon were like wolves. This is how I saw it, marked with the double ya’ from below, but it is with the unified ba’, and that is a typo, and God knows best. The point is that Solomon, peace be upon him, understood her words and smiled, laughing at that, and this is a very serious matter. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Abu Al-Siddiq Al-Naji, who said: Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both, went out to pray for rain, and there he saw an ant lying on its back, raising its legs to the sky and saying: O God, we are one of Your creations, and we cannot do without Your rain, and if You do not rain on us, we will perish. Solomon said: Go back, for you have been watered by the supplication of someone other than yourselves. It was proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “An ant bit one of the prophets, so he ordered the ant colony to be burned. Then God revealed to him: ‘Because an ant bit you, did you destroy a nation of nations that glorify God? Why not just one ant?’”
27:19: God the Almighty tells us about the abundant blessings, sublime gifts, and beautiful attributes He bestowed upon His servants and prophets: David and his son Solomon, peace be upon them, and what He combined for them between the happiness of this world and the hereafter, and the kingdom and complete empowerment in this world, and the prophethood and message in religion. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, 'Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.' Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yahya bin Tamam, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather, who said: Omar bin Abdul Aziz wrote: God does not bestow a blessing upon a servant for whom he praises God, except that his praise is better than his blessing. If only you could have known that from the revealed Book of God. God the Almighty said: And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, 'Praise be to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants.' So what blessing is better than what was given to David and Solomon, peace be upon them. And the Almighty’s saying: And Solomon inherited David means in the kingdom and prophethood. What is meant is not the inheritance of wealth, because if that were the case, Solomon would not have been singled out from among the rest of David’s sons, since David had one hundred wives. Rather, what is meant by that is the inheritance of the kingdom and prophethood, because the wealth of the prophets is not inherited, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us in his saying: “We, the prophets, are not inherited. What we leave behind is charity.” And he said: O people, we have been taught the language of birds and have been given of all things. That is, he informed Solomon of God’s blessings upon him in what He bestowed upon him of complete kingdom and great empowerment, to the point that He subjected to him mankind, jinn, and birds, and he also knew the language of birds and animals. This is something that no human being was given, according to what we know of what God and His Messenger informed us of. And whoever among the ignorant and common folk claims that animals spoke like the speech of the sons of Adam before Solomon, son of David, as many people may utter, then this is a statement without knowledge. And if that were the case, then singling Solomon out would have been of no benefit, since all of them hear the speech of birds and animals, and know what She says, "It is not as they claimed or said. Rather, the animals, birds, and all other creatures have been in this form and manner since they were created until our time. 27:20: Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and others said on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others: The hoopoe was an engineer who used to guide Solomon, peace be upon him, to water if it was in a deserted area, so he would look for it. The water would look for him at the edges of the earth, just as a person sees something that appears on the surface of the earth, and he knows how far it is from the surface of the earth. So when he guided them to it, Solomon, peace be upon him, ordered the jinn to dig for him that place so that he could extract the water from its bottom. So Solomon, peace be upon him, went down one day to a deserted area and inspected the birds to see the hoopoe, but he did not see it. He said, ‘Why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?’ One day Abdullah bin Abbas told something similar to this. Among the people was a man from the Khawarij called Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq, who often objected to Ibn Abbas. So he said to him, Stop, Ibn Abbas, you have been defeated today. He said, Why? He said: You say about the hoopoe that he sees water on the edges of the earth, and that the boy puts a seed in the trap for him and throws dirt on the trap, then the hoopoe comes to take it and falls into the trap and the boy catches him. Ibn Abbas said: If this had not gone and said: I replied to Ibn Abbas, I would not have answered him. Then he said to him: Woe to you, when the decree descends, sight becomes blind and caution is lost. Nafi’ said to him: By God, I will never argue with you about anything in the Qur’an. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Abu Abdullah Al-Barzi from the people of Barzah in the Ghouta of Damascus, that he was one of the righteous who fasted on Mondays and Thursdays, and he was one-eyed and had reached the age of eighty. Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Abu Sulayman bin Zayd that he asked him about the reason for his blindness, and he refused, so he insisted on him for months, and he told him that two men from the people of Khorasan stayed with him one Friday in the village of Barzah, and they asked him about a valley there, so he showed it to them. They brought out incense burners and lit a lot of incense in them until the valley was filled with smoke, and they began to incense while snakes came to them from every direction, and they did not pay attention to any of them, until a snake approached the distance of an arm and its eyes were burning like a dinar, so they were very happy about it, and they said, Praise be to God who did not disappoint our journey in a year. They broke the incense burners and took the snake, and they put a mile in its eye and applied it to their kohl, so I asked them to apply it to me, but they refused, so I insisted on them and said: No. Instead, I threatened them with the state, so they blackened my right eye, and when it fell into my eye, I looked at the ground beneath me like a mirror, seeing what was beneath it as a mirror sees. Then they said to me: Walk with them a little, so I walked with them and they talked to me until I was far from the village, then they took me and bound me, and one of them put his hand into my eye and gouged it out and threw it away and they went on, so I remained like that, bound until a group of people passed by and untied me, and this is what happened to my eye. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Sadaqah bin Amr Al-Ghasani told us, Ibad bin Maysarah Al-Manqari told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The name of the hoopoe of Solomon, peace be upon him, was Anbar. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When Solomon, peace be upon him, went out to the place where he used to sit, he would check on the birds. They claim that every kind of bird would come to him every day, so he looked and saw all kinds of birds present except the hoopoe. He said, ‘Why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent ones?’ Did my sight miss him from the birds, or was he absent and not present? And His statement: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment. Al-A'mash said, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means plucking his feathers. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: He will pluck his feathers and expose him to the sun. And more than one of the early Muslims said the same, that he plucked his feathers and left him lying down to be eaten by ants and midges. And His statement: Or I will slaughter him, means killing him, or he brings me clear authority, with a clear and obvious excuse. Sufyan bin Uyaynah and Abdullah bin Shaddad said: When the hoopoe came, the birds said to him: What kept you? Solomon vowed to kill you. He said: Did he make an exception? They said: Yes. He said: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he brings me clear authority. He said: Then you are saved. Mujahid said: God only protected him because of his kindness to his mother.

27:22: God Almighty says: So he stayed the hoopoe not long meaning he was absent for a short time, then he came and said to Solomon: I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed meaning I have seen that which you and your soldiers have not seen and I have come to you from Sheba with certain report meaning with true, real, certain report, and Sheba is Himyar and they are the kings of Yemen, then he said: Indeed, I have found a woman ruling over them Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: She is Bilqis bint Shuraheel, the Queen of Sheba. Qatada said: Her mother was a jinn, and the back of her feet was like the hoof of an animal from the house of a kingdom. Zuhair bin Muhammad said: She is Bilqis bint Shuraheel bin Malik bin Al-Rayyan, and her mother is Far’ah the jinn. Ibn Jurayj said: Bilqis bint Dhi Sharkh and her mother is Balta’ah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Musaddad told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were with the companion of Solomon a thousand qails, under each qail a hundred thousand fighters. Al-A’mash said: On the authority of Mujahid, there were under the control of the Queen of Sheba twelve thousand qails, under each qail a hundred thousand fighters. Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the words of God Almighty: I found a woman ruling them, she was from a royal family, and her advisors were three hundred and twelve men, each man over ten thousand men, and she was in a land called Ma’rib, three miles from Sana’a. This statement is more likely to be a lot for the kingdom of Yemen, and God knows best. His statement: And she has been given of all things meaning of the worldly pleasures that a powerful king needs. And she has a mighty throne meaning a huge bed on which she sits, decorated with gold and all kinds of jewels and pearls. Zuhair ibn Muhammad said: It was made of gold and its panels were lined with rubies and chrysolite. Its length was eighty cubits and its width was forty cubits. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was made of gold inlaid with rubies, chrysolite and pearls. Only women served her, and she had six hundred women in charge of her service. Historians said: This bed was in a huge, lofty, and well-built palace. It had three hundred and sixty windows in its east and a similar number in its west. Its construction was arranged so that the sun would enter from one window every day and set opposite it, so they would prostrate to it morning and evening. For this reason, God said: She found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God, and Satan had made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the way meaning from the path of truth so they are not guided. His statement: that they should not prostrate to God means, “And Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, so they are not guided. That they should not prostrate to God” meaning they do not know the path of truth, which is to sincerely prostrate to God alone, without what He created of planets and others, as God the Most High said: “And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God, who created them, if you should worship Him.” Some of the reciters read, that they should not prostrate to God, making it the opening ala and the ya for the call, and the vocative was deleted, meaning, O my people, prostrate to God. And His statement: Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He knows every hidden thing in the heaven and the earth. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and others said. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: The hidden thing is water. This is what Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The hidden thing in the heavens and the earth is what He has placed within them of provisions: rain from the sky and vegetation from the earth. This is appropriate from the words of the hoopoe, in which God endowed with the characteristic mentioned by Ibn Abbas and others, that he sees water running within the boundaries of the earth and within it. And His statement: And He knows what you conceal and what you declare meaning, He knows what His servants conceal and what they declare of words and deeds. This is like His statement: It is the same among you whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud, whether you hide it by night or go forth by day and His statement: God - there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne meaning, He is the One called upon, and He is God, there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne, than whom there is no creation greater. Since the hoopoe calls to goodness, to the worship of God alone and to prostrate to Him, it was forbidden to kill it, as narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade the killing of four types of creatures: the ant, the bee, the hoopoe, and the shrike", and its chain of transmission is authentic.

27:32: When she read to them the letter of Solomon, she consulted them about her situation and what had happened to her. For this reason, she said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide on a matter until you witness it." That is, until you are present and consult. They said, 'We are men of strength and of great might.' That is, they presented their numbers, numbers, and strength to her. Then they entrusted the matter to her after that, saying, And the matter is in your hands, so consider what you command. That is, we have no problem with it and we have no problem if you wish to go after him and fight him, for we have no problem with it. After this, the matter is in your hands. Give us your opinion, and we will comply with it and obey it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, said: They entrusted their affair to a woman whose breasts were trembling. When they said to her what they said, she was more decisive than them and more knowledgeable about the matter of Solomon, and that she would not be able to face his soldiers and armies and what he had subjected to him of jinn, humans, and birds. She witnessed something amazing and wonderful in the case of the book with the hoopoe, so she said to them: I fear that if we fight him and resist him, he will target us with his soldiers and destroy us and those with him, and he will end up destroying and ruining me and you, and not anyone else. That is why she said: When kings enter a town, they corrupt it Ibn Abbas said: That is, if they enter a country by force, they corrupt it, that is, they destroy it. And they make the most honored of its people humiliated that is, they target the governors and soldiers in it and humiliate them to the utmost degree, either by killing or capturing them. Ibn Abbas said: Bilqis said, When kings enter a town, they corrupt it and make the most honorable of its people humiliated. The Lord Almighty said, And thus they do. Then she turned to reconciliation, truce, peacemaking, deception and flattery, and said, And indeed, I will send to them a gift and see with what the messengers return. That is, I will send him a gift befitting someone like him and see what his response will be after that. Perhaps he will accept it from us and refrain from fighting us, or impose a tax on us that we will pay to him every year and commit to it, and he will stop fighting and waging war against us. Qatada may God have mercy on him said: How wise she was in her Islam and polytheism. She knew that gifts are accepted by people. Ibn Abbas and others said: She said to her people, “If he accepts the gift, then he is a king, so fight him. But if he does not accept it, then he is a prophet, so follow him.”

27:36: More than one of the commentators from the Salaf and others mentioned that she sent him a great gift of gold, jewels, pearls and other things. Some of them said: She sent him a brick of gold, but the correct view is that she sent him a vessel of gold. Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said: She sent female slaves dressed as boys, and male slaves dressed as female slaves, and she said: If he distinguishes these from those, then he is a prophet. They said: So Solomon ordered them to perform ablution, and the female slave poured water over her hand and the male slave scooped up water, thus distinguishing them. It was also said that she made the female slave wash the palms of her hands before the backs of them, and the male slaves did the opposite. It was also said that she made the female slaves wash from their palms to their elbows, and the male slaves wash from their elbows to their palms. There is no contradiction between all of that, and God knows best. Some of them mentioned that she sent him a cup to fill with pure water, neither from the sky nor from the earth. He made the horses run until they sweated, then he filled it with that, and with a bead and a wire to put in it, and he did that - and God knows best whether that was the case or not. Most of it is taken from the Israelite traditions. It appears that Solomon, peace be upon him, did not look at what they had brought at all, nor did he care about it, but rather ignored it. He said, denouncing them, Do you provide me with wealth? That is, Do you pretend to give me wealth so that I will leave you in your polytheism and your kingdom? “But what God has given me is better than what He has given you.” That is, what God has given me of kingdom, wealth, and soldiers is better than what you have. Rather, you rejoice in your gifts. That is, you are the ones who are led by gifts and presents, but as for me, I will not accept from you anything but Islam or the sword. Al-A'mash narrated from Al-Munhal bin Amr from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him: “Solomon ordered the devils to fake for him a thousand palaces of gold and silver. When their messengers saw that, they said, ‘What is this doing with our gift?’ This indicates the permission for kings to prepare themselves and show off their adornments to messengers and visitors. ‘Return to them’ meaning with their gift, ‘and we will surely come to them with soldiers they will not be able to withstand’ meaning they will not have the strength to fight them, ‘and we will surely expel them from it humiliated’ meaning we will expel them from their city humiliated, ‘while they are degraded’ meaning humiliated and defeated. When her messengers returned to her with her gift and what Solomon had said, she and her people heard and obeyed, and she and her people came to him with her soldiers, submissive and humbled, honoring Solomon and intending to follow him in Islam. When Solomon (peace be upon him) confirmed their arrival and delegation to him, he was happy and pleased with that.

27:38: Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman, who said: When the messengers returned to her with what Solomon had said, she said: By God, I know that this is not a king, and that we have no power over him and that we will not do anything by defying him. She sent to him: I am coming to you with the kings of my people to see what you command and what you call us to of your religion. Then she ordered her royal bed on which she used to sit to be brought. It was made of gold, inlaid with rubies, emeralds, and pearls. It was placed in seven chambers, one inside the other. Then the doors were locked and she said to the one she left in charge of her kingdom: Keep what is before you and my royal throne, so that none of God’s servants may reach it, and no one may see it until I come to you. Then she went to Solomon with twelve thousand Qil of the kings of Yemen, under the command of each Qil of them were many thousands. So Solomon began to send the jinn to bring him information about her journey and her destination every day and night until she drew near, he gathered the jinn and humans who were under his command and said: O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? Qatada said: When Sulayman heard that she was kneeling, and her throne had been mentioned to him, he was impressed. It was made of gold and its legs were made of pearls and jewels. It was covered with brocade and silk, and had nine locks. He disliked taking it after their conversion to Islam. The Prophet of God knew that when they converted to Islam, their money and blood would be sacred, so he said, O eminent ones, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me as Muslims? This is what Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, and Zuhayr ibn Muhammad said: Before they come to me as Muslims, so their money would be sacred to me because of their conversion to Islam. An ‘Ifrit from the jinn said, Mujahid said: meaning a rebel from the jinn. Shu’ayb al-Jubba’i said: His name was Kuzan. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said the same on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, and Wahb ibn Munabbih also said the same. Abu Salih said: It was like a mountain. I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: meaning before you rise from your seat. Mujahid said: Your seat. Al-Suddi and others said: He used to sit for people for judgments, government affairs and food, from the beginning of the day until the sun set. And indeed, I am for this strong and trustworthy. Ibn Abbas said: That is, strong to carry it and trustworthy for what is in it of substance. So Solomon, peace be upon him, said: I want something faster than that. From here it becomes clear that Solomon wanted to bring this throne to demonstrate the greatness of what God had given him of kingship and the soldiers He had subjected to him, which no one before him and will be given to anyone after him. And to take that as evidence of his prophethood to Bilqis and her people, because this is a great miracle, to bring her throne as it is from her country before they come to it, and she had hidden it with locks, padlocks and guards. So when Solomon said: I want something faster than that, He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, Ibn Abbas said: He was Asaf, Solomon’s scribe. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman that he was Asaf ibn Barkhiya. He was a truthful person who knew the Greatest Name. Qatada said: He was a believing human being named Asif. Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak and Qatada also said that he was human. Qatada added: From the Children of Israel. Mujahid said his name was Astum. Qatada said in a narration from him: His name was Bulaykha. Zuhair ibn Muhammad said: He was a human being called Dhu al-Nur. Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah claimed that he was Al-Khidr, but this is very strange. And His statement: "I will bring it to you before you blink" meaning, raise your gaze and look, extend your gaze as far as you can, for your sight will not tire except with it present to you. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Extend your gaze, for it will not reach its limit until I bring it to you. They mentioned that he ordered him to look towards Yemen, where this desired throne is. Then he stood up, performed ablution, and supplicated to God. Mujahid said: He said: O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Az-Zuhri said: He said: O our God and the God of all things, One God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne. He said: It appeared before him. Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, and others said: When he supplicated to God and asked Him to bring him the throne of Bilqis, and he was in Yemen and Solomon, peace be upon him, was in Jerusalem, the throne disappeared and sank into the ground, then it sprang up from before Solomon. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Solomon did not feel anything until her throne was being carried in his hands. He said: This was what he brought from the sea worshippers. When Solomon and his people saw it and saw it settled near him, he said: This is from the bounty of my Lord meaning this is from the blessings of God upon me to test me meaning to examine me “whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself” like His saying: Whoever does righteousness does so for his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it and like His saying: And whoever does righteousness prepares for themselves. And His statement: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous. That is, He is Free of need of His servants and their worship, and Generous, meaning Generous in Himself, even if no one worships Him, for His greatness is not in need of anyone. This is like what Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy. And in Sahih Muslim: “God the Most High says: O My servants, were the first and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you to be as pious as the most wicked heart of any man among you, that would not increase My dominion in the least. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you and then recompense you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.”

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman that he was Asaf ibn Barkhiya. He was a truthful person who knew the Greatest Name. Qatada said: He was a believing human being named Asif. Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak and Qatada also said that he was human. Qatada added: From the Children of Israel. Mujahid said his name was Astum. Qatada said in a narration from him: His name was Bulaykha. Zuhair ibn Muhammad said: He was a human being called Dhu al-Nur. Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah claimed that he was Al-Khidr, but this is very strange. And His statement: I will bring it to you before you blink meaning, raise your gaze and look, extend your gaze as far as you can, for your sight will not tire except with it present to you. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Extend your gaze, for it will not reach its limit until I bring it to you. They mentioned that he ordered him to look towards Yemen, where this desired throne is. Then he stood up, performed ablution, and supplicated to God. Mujahid said: He said: O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Az-Zuhri said: He said: O our God and the God of all things, One God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne. He said: It appeared before him. Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, and others said: When he supplicated to God and asked Him to bring him the throne of Bilqis, and he was in Yemen and Solomon, peace be upon him, was in Jerusalem, the throne disappeared and sank into the ground, then it sprang up from before Solomon. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: Solomon did not feel anything until her throne was being carried in his hands. He said: This was what he brought from the sea worshippers. When Solomon and his people saw it and saw it settled near him, he said: This is from the bounty of my Lord meaning this is from the blessings of God upon me to test me meaning to examine me “whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself” like His saying: Whoever does righteousness does so for his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it and like His saying: And whoever does righteousness prepares for themselves. And His statement: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous. That is, He is Free of need of His servants and their worship, and Generous, meaning Generous in Himself, even if no one worships Him, for His greatness is not in need of anyone. This is like what Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy. And in Sahih Muslim: “God the Most High says: O My servants, were the first and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you to be as pious as the most wicked heart of any man among you, that would not increase My dominion in the least. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you and then recompense you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.”

27:41: When the throne of Bilqis was brought to Solomon, peace be upon him, before her arrival, he ordered that some of its features be changed to test her knowledge and steadfastness upon seeing it, to see whether she would accept that it was her throne or not. He said, "Disguise her throne for her; we will see whether she will be guided or whether she will be among those who are not guided. Ibn Abbas said, He removed its jewels and its sides. Mujahid said, He ordered that what was red be made yellow, what was yellow be made red, and what was green be made red, changing everything from its original state. Ikrimah said, They added to it and took away from it. Qatada said, He made its bottom its top and its front its back, and they added to it and took away from it. So when she came, it was said, 'Is this your throne?'" That is, her throne was presented to her, changed and distorted, and things were added to and taken away from it. But she was steadfast and intelligent, and she had intelligence, cunning, and resolve. She did not accept that it was hers because of its great distance from her, nor did she accept that it was another one because she saw its effects and features, even though it had been changed, altered, and distorted. So she said, "It is as if it were it," meaning it resembles it and is close to it. This is very smart and decisive. And his saying: And We were given knowledge before her, and we were Muslims. Mujahid said that Sulayman said it. And the saying of God Almighty: “And that which she worshipped besides God prevented her. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.” This is from the completion of the words of Sulayman, peace be upon him, in the saying of Mujahid and Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may God have mercy on them, meaning Sulayman said: And We were given knowledge before her, and we were Muslims. And she had been prevented, that is, prevented from worshipping God alone, “that which she worshipped besides God. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.” This is what Mujahid and Sa’id said: It is good, and Ibn Jarir also said it. Then Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that in his saying and prevented her there is a pronoun referring to Sulayman or to God Almighty, and its meaning is that He prevented her that which she worshipped besides God meaning He prevented her from worshipping other than God that she was from a disbelieving people. I say: And what Mujahid said is supported by the fact that she only declared Islam after entering the palace, as will come. And his saying: She was told, ‘Enter the palace.’ When she saw it, she thought it was a sea, and uncovered her legs. This is because Solomon, peace be upon him, ordered the devils to build her a great palace of glass, and water ran underneath it. Someone who did not know would think it was water, but the glass stood between the one walking and it. They differed about the reason that prompted Solomon, peace be upon him, to build it. It was said that when he decided to marry her and choose her for himself, her beauty and handsomeness were mentioned to him, but on her legs was a large bald spot, and the back of her feet was like the back of an animal. This displeased him, so he built this to see if it was true or not. This is what Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and others said. When she entered and uncovered her legs, he saw the most beautiful legs and feet of people, but he saw hair on her feet because she was a queen and had no husband. He wanted to remove that from her, so she was told the razor, but she said, I cannot do that. Solomon disliked this and said to the jinn, Make something other than the razor that will remove this hair. So they made him a paste. He was the first to make a paste for himself, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and others. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman, then he said to her: Enter the palace so that he may show her a kingdom more honorable than her kingdom and a power greater than her power. When she saw it, she thought it was a sea and uncovered her legs, not doubting that it was water in which she was wading. She was told that it was a palace made of smooth glass. When she stood before Solomon, he called her to worship God alone and rebuked her for worshipping the sun instead of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: When the foreign woman saw the palace, she knew, by God, that she had seen a king greater than her kingdom. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of some of the people of knowledge on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: Solomon ordered the palace and the devils had made it for him from glass, as white as water. Then he sent water beneath it and placed his bed in it, so he sat on it and the birds, jinn, and humans clung to it. Then he said to her: Enter the palace so that he may show her a kingdom more honorable than her kingdom and a power greater than her power. When she saw it, she thought it was a sea and uncovered her legs, not doubting that it was water in which she was wading. She was told: It is a palace made of smooth glass. Bottles. When she stood before Solomon, he called her to worship God Almighty alone and rebuked her for worshipping the sun instead of God. She said what the heretics say, so Solomon fell down in prostration in awe of what she said, and the people prostrated with him. She fell at her hands when she saw Solomon doing what he did. When Solomon raised his head, he said, Woe to you, what did you say? She said, Have you forgotten what I said? She said, My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds. So she submitted, and her submission was good. Imam Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated a strange hadith on this from Ibn Abbas, saying: Al-Husayn bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaydah, who told me, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, who told us, on the authority of Mujahid, while we were in Al-Azd, who said: Ibn Abbas told us: Solomon, peace be upon him, would sit on his throne, then chairs would be placed around him, and the humans would sit on them, then the jinn would sit, then the devils, then the wind would come and lift them up, then the birds would shade them, then they would go out in the morning for as long as a traveler would like to dismount, a month, and in the evening for a month. He said: One day, while he was on a journey, he looked for the birds and he missed the hoopoe, so he said: Why do I not see the hoopoe, or is he among the absent? * I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me clear authority. He said: And his punishment for him was that he would pluck him out and throw him on the ground, so that he would not be protected from an ant or any of the vermin of the earth. Ata' said: Sa'id bin Jubair mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas something like the hadith of Mujahid: "So he stayed not long" and he read until he reached the verse: "We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars. Go with this letter of mine and he wrote in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, to Bilqis that you not exalt yourselves over me and come to me in submission" When the hoopoe threw the letter to her, it was cast into her mind that it was a noble letter and that it was from Solomon and that you not exalt yourselves over me and come to me in submission. They said, "We are men of strength. She said, Indeed, when kings enter a town, they corrupt it. And I am going to send them a gift to see what the messengers will bring back. When the gift came to Solomon, he said, Do you provide me with money so that I may return to them?" When he looked at the dust, Ibn Abbas informed us. He said, "And between Solomon and the Queen of Sheba and those with her when he looked at the dust was like what is between us and al-Hirah. Ata' and Mujahid said, At that time, it was with the Azd. Solomon said, Which of you will bring me her throne? He said, Between her throne and Solomon when he looked at the dust was a distance of two months' journey. An Ifrit from the jinn said, 'I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat.'" Solomon had a council in which he would sit for the people as rulers sit, then he would stand up. He said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat. Solomon said, I want something faster than that. The one who had knowledge of the Scripture said, I will look in the Book of my Lord, then I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." Solomon looked at him, and when he finished speaking, Solomon looked again, and her throne sprang up from under Solomon's feet, from under a chair on which Solomon would place his feet and then climb onto the bed. He said, "When Solomon saw her throne, he said, 'This is from the bounty of my Lord.' The verse, He said, 'They denied her throne to her.' So when she came, it was said, Is this your throne? She said, It is as if it were the same." So when she came to him, she asked him about two things. She said to Solomon, "I want water that is not from the earth or the sky." When Solomon was asked about something, he would ask the humans, then the jinn, then the devils. The devils said, This is an easy reward for horses, then take their sweat and fill vessels with it. So he ordered the horses to be made to run, then he took their sweat and filled vessels with it. He said, And you asked about the color of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Solomon jumped from his bed and fell down in prostration and said, O Lord, you have asked me about a matter that is too great for me to mention to you. God said, Go back, for I have sufficed you against them. He said, So he returned to his bed. He said, What did you ask about? She said, I only asked you about water. He said to his soldiers, What did you ask about? They said, I only asked you about water. He said, And they all forgot about it. He said, The devils said, ‘Solomon wants to take her for himself, but if he takes her for himself and a child is born to them, we will never be free from his slavery.’ So they made a smooth palace of glass in which were fish. It was said to her, Enter the palace. When she saw it, she thought it was a sea, and she uncovered her legs, and behold, they were hairy. Solomon said, This is ugly, so how can it be removed? They said: The razor removes it. He said: The mark of the razor is ugly. He said: So the devils made the light. He said: He was the first for whom the light was made. Then Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: What a beautiful hadith! I said: Rather, it is a very strange and strange fabrication, and perhaps it is from the delusions of Ata bin Al-Saib against Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. The most likely interpretation in such contexts is that it was received from the People of the Book from what was found in their scriptures, such as the narrations of Ka’b and Wahb, may God forgive them, in what they conveyed to this nation of the report of the Children of Israel, of the eternal, the strange, and the marvelous, what was and what was not, and what was distorted, changed, and abrogated. God, the Exalted, has enriched us with what is more correct, more beneficial, clearer, and more eloquent, all praise and thanks be to God. The root of the word sarh in Arabic speech is a palace or any tall building. God, the Exalted, said, informing about Pharaoh, may God curse him, that he said to his minister Haman, Build for me a tower that I may reach the causes the verse. Al-Sarh is a high-construction palace in Yemen, and Al-Mamard is the one built with a solid, smooth construction of bottles, meaning glass. Tamrid of construction means smoothing it, and Mard is a fortress in Dumat Al-Jandal. The purpose is that Solomon, peace be upon him, built a great, lofty palace of glass for this queen to show her the greatness of his authority and his power. When she saw what God had given him and the majesty of what he was in and had insight into his matter, she submitted to the command of God Almighty and knew that he was a noble prophet and a great king. She submitted to God Almighty and said, My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, meaning by what came before of her disbelief, polytheism, and her and her people’s worship of the sun instead of God, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds, meaning following the religion of Solomon in his worship of God alone, with no partner who created everything and determined it with a precise determination.

Then they would say to his close relatives that they did not know anything about his affair, and that they were truthful in what they told them that they had not witnessed that. So God the Almighty said: And there were in the city meaning the city of Thamud nine men meaning nine men who were spreading corruption in the land and were not reforming. These people were the ones who prevailed over the affair of Thamud because they were their leaders and chiefs. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: These are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel, meaning those who did that based on their own opinion and consultation. May God curse them and make them ugly, and He did that. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The names of these nine were: Dhumi, Du’aim, Haram, Harim, Dab, Sawab, Riyab, Masta’, and Qadar bin Salaf, the one who hamstrung the she-camel, i.e. the one who did that with his own hand. God Almighty said: So they called to their companion, and he seized the camel and hamstrung it. And God Almighty said: When the most wretched of them arose. Abdul Razzaq said: Yahya bin Rabi’ah al-San’ani informed us, I heard Ata’ - who is Ibn Abi Rabah - say, There were nine men in Madinah who spread corruption on earth and did not reform. He said: They used to lend dirhams, meaning they used to take from them as if they were dealing with them by number as the Arabs did. Imam Malik reported from Yahya bin Sa’id from Sa’id bin al-Musayyab that he said: Cutting up gold and paper is a form of corruption on earth. In the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and others: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade breaking the coins of Muslims that were in circulation except for a reason. The point is that one of the characteristics of these disbelieving sinners was to spread corruption on earth in any way they could, and some of them are what these imams and others have mentioned. God the Almighty said: They said, ‘We will surely kill him and his family by night.’ That is, they allied and agreed to kill the Prophet of God Salih, peace be upon him, by whoever met him at night by treachery. But God plotted against them and turned the tables on them. Mujahid said: They allied and swore to kill him, but they did not reach him until they and all their people were destroyed. Qatada said: They allied themselves to capture him by night and kill him. It was mentioned to us that while they were embracing Salih to kill him, God sent a rock upon them that made them collapse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel. They said when they hamstrung it: We will surely kill Salih and his family by night and then say to the followers of Salih: We did not witness any of this, and we have no knowledge of it. So God destroyed them all. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: These nine said after they had hamstrung the she-camel: Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will join him with his she-camel. So they came to him at night to spend the night with his family, but the angels stoned them. When they delayed their companions, they came to Salih’s house and found them wounded and crushed with stones. They said to Salih: You killed them. Then they intended to attack him, but his clan stood up to protect him, put on their weapons, and said to them: By God, you will never kill him, for he promised you that the punishment would descend upon you in three days. If he is truthful, then do not increase your Lord’s wrath upon you, but if he is lying, then you will be behind what you want. So they left them that night. Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim said: When they hamstrung the she-camel, Salih said to them, “Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied.” They said, Salih claimed that he would be done with us in three days, so we will be done with him and his family before three. Salih had a mosque in al-Hijr near a valley there in which he prayed, so they went out to a cave, that is, a cavern there, at night and said, When he comes to pray, we will kill him, then when we are done with him, we will return to his family. So we were done with them. Then God sent a rock from the plateau opposite them, and they feared that it would crush them, so they hastened. The rock closed over them while they were in that cave, and their people did not know where they were, nor did they know what was done to their people. So God punished these here, and those there, and God saved Salih and those with him. Then he recited, “And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they perceived not. So see how was the end of their plot: We destroyed them and their people, all together. So those are their houses, empty,” that is, empty, with no one in them, “because of what they did. Indeed, in That is a sign for a people who know. And We saved those who believed and were fearing God.
27:54: God Almighty tells us about His servant and messenger Lot, peace be upon him, that he warned his people of God’s punishment against them for committing an immorality that no one among the children of Adam had committed before them, which is approaching males without females. This is a great immorality, as men are content with men, and women with women. He said: Do you commit immorality while you see? That is, you see each other, and you commit evil in your gatherings. Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly. That is, you do not know anything, neither by nature nor by law, as He said in the other verse: Do you approach males from among the worlds * and abandon what your Lord has created for you as mates? Rather, you are a transgressing people. “Then the answer of his people was only that they said, ‘Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.’” That is, they are wary of doing what you are doing and of approving of your actions. So expel them from among you, for they are not fit to live next to you in your country. So they resolved to do that. So God destroyed them and the disbelievers like them. God the Almighty said: {So We saved him and his family, except for his wife. We destined her to be among those who remained behind.} That is, among those who would perish with her people, because she was a support to them in their religion and their way, in her approval of their ugly actions. She used to guide her people to the guests of Lot so that they would come to them. She did not commit indecencies out of respect for the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), not out of respect for herself. God the Almighty said: {And We rained down upon them a rain.} That is, stones of layered baked clay, marked with your Lord, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. For this reason He said: {Evil was the rain of those who were warned.} That is, those against whom the proof was established and the warning reached them, but they disobeyed the Messenger and denied him and intended to expel him from their midst.
