27:59: God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say: Praise be to God, meaning for His countless blessings upon His servants, and for the sublime attributes and beautiful names with which He is described, and to send peace upon the servants of God whom He has chosen and selected, who are His noble Messengers and Prophets, upon them be the best of blessings and peace from God. This is what Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said: What is meant by His servants whom He has chosen are the prophets. He said: It is like His statement: "Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. And peace be upon the messengers. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds." Ath-Thawri and as-Suddi said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and may God be pleased with them all. A similar narration was also narrated from Ibn Abbas. There is no contradiction, for if they are among the servants of God whom He has chosen, then the prophets are even more so. The point is that God Almighty commanded His Messenger and those who followed him, after He mentioned to them what He did for His friends in terms of salvation, victory, and support, and what He brought upon His enemies in terms of humiliation, torment, and subjugation, to praise Him for all His actions and to send peace upon His chosen and good servants. Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Amara bin Subaih narrated to us, Talq bin Ghannam narrated to us, Al-Hakam bin Zuhair narrated to us, from Al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas, “And peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen,” he said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God chose for His Prophet, may God be pleased with them. And His statement, Is God better, or do they associate others with Him? is a question of denial of the polytheists for worshipping other gods with God. Then God Almighty proceeded to explain that He is the One alone in creation, provision, and management, and no one else, so He said, Or did He create the heavens? That is, He created those heavens in their height and clarity, and what He placed in them of luminous planets, shining stars, and revolving spheres. And He created the earth in its lowness and density, and what He placed in it of mountains, mountains, plains, rugged terrain, deserts, wastelands, crops, trees, fruits, seas, and animals of different kinds, shapes, colors, and other things. And the Almighty’s saying: And He has sent down for you from the sky water meaning He made it a provision for the servants and We caused to grow thereby gardens meaning orchards of delight meaning a beautiful sight and a beautiful form it was not for you to cause its trees to grow meaning you would not have been able to cause its trees to grow. Only the Creator, the Provider, who is independent in that and unique in that, is able to do that, without any idols or rivals besides Him, as these polytheists acknowledge as the Almighty said in another verse: And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ “And if you ask them, ‘Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’” That is, they acknowledge that He alone is the doer of all that, with no partner or associate. Yet they worship something else along with Him, which they acknowledge does not create or provide, but rather deserves to be singled out for worship. Who is the One who is unique in creation and provision? For this reason the Almighty said: Is there a god with God? meaning, is there a god with God who should be worshipped? It has become clear to you and to every intelligent person, from what they also acknowledge, that He is the Creator, the Provider. Some commentators say that the meaning of His statement, Is there a god with God? is that He did this, and this goes back to the meaning of the first, because the answer is understood to be that they say there is no one who did this with Him, but He is the One who is unique in it. So it is said, How can you worship someone other than Him while He is the Independent, the One who is unique in creation, provision, and management? As God the Almighty said, Is He who creates like one who does not create? Al-An’am 2:17. And His statement here, Is He who created the heavens and the earth? “Is He who” in all these verses means is He who does these things like one who is not able to do any of them? This is the meaning of the context, even though the other is not mentioned, because the force of the speech indicates that. God the Almighty said, Is God better or what they associate with Him? Then He said in the other verse: Rather, they are a people who are just, meaning they attribute to God justice and a counterpart. And thus the Almighty said: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? That is, is he like this like one who is not like this? And for this reason the Almighty said: Say, ‘Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only those of understanding will remember.’ “Is one whose breast God has expanded to Islam so that he is upon light from his Lord? Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God? Those are in clear error.” And the Almighty said: Is one who is watchful over every soul for what it has earned? That is, is he who is a witness over the actions of creation, their movements and their stillness, and knows the unseen, both great and small, like one who does not know, hear, or see, of these idols that they worshipped besides God? And for this reason He said: “And they have attributed to God partners. Say, ‘Name them.’” And so on in all these noble verses.

27:61: The Almighty says: Is He who has made the earth a resting place? That is, a stable, motionless continent that does not shake or tremble with its inhabitants? If it were like that, life and existence would not be pleasant on it. Rather, He made it, out of His grace and mercy, a stable, rugged bed that does not shake or move, as the Almighty said in the other verse: God is He who made the earth a resting place for you and the sky a canopy. “And placed within it rivers.” That is, He placed within it fresh, good rivers, splitting them in its midst and distributing them between large and small rivers, and between that, and making them flow east, west, south, and north according to the interests of His servants in their regions and countries, urging their dispersal throughout the earth and providing them with their provisions according to what they need. And placed for it firm mountains. That is, towering mountains that anchor the earth and make it firm so that it does not shake with them. And placed between the two seas a barrier. That is, He placed between the fresh and salty waters a barrier, that is, an obstacle that prevents them from mixing so that one does not spoil the other, and the other is by this, for the divine wisdom It requires that each of them be judged in its intended manner. The fresh sea is these free-flowing rivers flowing among people, and the purpose of them is to be sweet and clear so that animals, plants and fruits can drink from them. The salty seas are those surrounding areas and regions from every side, and the purpose of them is for their water to be salty and bitter so that the air is not spoiled by their smell, as God the Almighty said: “And it is He who has released the two seas, one fresh and sweet, and the other salty and bitter. And He placed between them a barrier and an insurmountable partition.” For this reason God the Almighty said: Is there a deity with God? That is, did He do this, or is He worshipped according to the first and last statement? Both are inseparable and correct. But most of them do not know, that is, in their worship of other than Him.
27:62: God the Almighty points out that He is the One called upon in times of hardship, the One hoped for in times of calamity, as He the Almighty said: And when harm touches you at sea, lost are those you call upon except Him and He the Almighty said: Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help and thus He said here Who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him? meaning who is the One to whom the distressed one turns except, and the One who does not remove the harm of the afflicted except Him. Imam Ahmad said: Affan informed us: Wahib informed us, Khalid al-Hadha’ informed us on the authority of Abu Tamima al-Hujaymi, on the authority of a man from Balhajim who said: I said, O Messenger of God, to whom do you call? He said: “I call upon God alone, who, if you are afflicted with harm, you call upon Him, He will remove it from you. And who, if you are lost in a barren land, you call upon Him, He will return it to you. And who, if you are afflicted with famine, you call upon Him, He will grow for you.” I said: Advise me. He said: “Do not curse anyone, and do not neglect doing good deeds, even if it is to meet your brother with a cheerful face, or to empty your bucket into the vessel of the person drawing water. Wrap your garment to the middle of your shin, and if you refuse, then to the ankles. And beware of letting the garment hang down, for letting the garment hang down is a sign of arrogance, and God does not like arrogance.” Imam Ahmad narrated it from another chain of transmission, and he mentioned the name of the companion and said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Yunus - he is Ibn Ubayd - told us, Ubaydah Al-Hujaymi told us, on the authority of Abu Tamimah Al-Hujaymi, on the authority of Jabir bin Salim Al-Hujaymi, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was wearing a cloak, and its hem had fallen over his feet. I said: ‘Which of you is Muhammad, the Messenger of God?’ He pointed to himself, so I said: ‘O Messenger of God, I am from the people of the desert and I am harsh with them, so advise me.’ He said: ‘Do not belittle any good deed, even if it is meeting your brother with a cheerful face, or emptying your bucket into the vessel of the person drawing water. If someone curses you for something he knows about you, do not curse him for something you know about him, for you will have his reward and he will bear his burden. Beware of letting your lower garment trail, for letting your lower garment trail is a sign of conceit, and God does not like conceit. Do not curse anyone.’” He said: So I did not curse anyone after that, not even a sheep or a camel. Abu Dawood and Al-Nasa’i narrated this hadith through various chains of transmission, and they have a valid part of it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Hashim told us, Abda bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Salih, who said: Tawus came to visit me, so I said to him: Pray to God for me, O Abu Abd Al-Rahman. He said: Pray for yourself, for He answers the one in need when he calls upon Him. Wahb bin Munabbih said: I read in the first book that God Almighty says: By My glory, whoever holds fast to Me, then the heavens and those in them plot against him, and the earths and those in them plot against him, then I will make for him a way out from between them. And whoever does not hold fast to Me, then I will cause the earth to swallow him up from beneath his feet and place him in the air and eat him up. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of a man narrated by Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Dawud Al-Daynuri, known as Al-Daqqi Al-Sufi, that this man said: I was renting on a mule of mine from Damascus to the town of Al-Zabadani, and one time a man rode with me, and we passed by on some of the road, on an untraveled road, so he said to me: Take this one, for it is closer. I said: I have no experience with it. He said: Rather It is closer, so we took it and came to a rough place and a deep valley in which there were many dead people. He said to me, Hold the mule’s head until I come down. So he came down, rolled up his sleeves, gathered his clothes, and drew a knife and headed towards me. I fled from him and he followed me. I implored him by God and said, Take the mule and what is on it. He said to me, I only want to kill you. I frightened him by God and by the punishment, but he refused. So I surrendered before him and said, If you see fit to leave me until I pray two rak’ahs, so he said, Hurry up. So I stood up to pray and the Quran faltered in my mind, and I could not remember a single letter of it. I remained standing bewildered, and he said, Hey, finish. Then God put into my tongue the words of God Almighty: Who answers the distressed when he calls upon Him and removes evil? Then I saw a horseman approaching from the mouth of the valley with a spear in his hand. He threw it at the man, but it did not miss his heart, and he fell dead. I clung to the horseman and said, By God, who are you? He said, I am the messenger of He who answers the distressed when he calls upon Him and removes evil. He said: So I took the mule and the load and returned safely. It was mentioned in the biography of Fatima bint Al-Hassan Umm Ahmad Al-Ajila that she said: One day the infidels defeated the Muslims in a raid, and a good horse stopped with his companion, who was wealthy and righteous. He said to the horse: What is the matter with you? Woe to you, I was only preparing you for a day like this. The horse said to him: Why should I not hold back while you entrust the fodder to the keepers, so they wrong me and feed me only a little? He said: I swear by God that after this day I will not feed you except in my lap. The horse ran at that moment and escaped its owner. After that, he was not fed except in his lap. His story became well known among the people and they began to go to him to hear about it. The report reached the Roman king, who said: No town can tolerate this man. He plotted to capture him in his own town, so he sent one of his apostates to him. When he reached him, he showed him that he had good intentions towards Islam and his people until he was assured. Then one day they went out walking along the coast. He had made an appointment with another person from the Roman king to help them capture him. When they surrounded him to capture him, he raised his eyes to the sky and said: O God, he has only deceived me with You, so protect me from them however You wish. Two lions came out and captured them, and the man returned safely. And the Almighty’s saying: And He will make you successors on the earth means that He will replace one generation with another generation and one successor with another, as the Almighty said: If He wills, He can take you away and replace you with whomever He wills, just as He created you from the offspring of another people. And the Almighty said: And it is He who made you successors on the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees. And the Almighty said: And when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am going to place on the earth a successive authority,’ meaning a people who will succeed one another, as we have explained previously. And this is how this verse is. And He will make you successors on the earth meaning nation after nation, generation after generation, and people after people. If He willed, He would have created them all at one time, and He would not have made some of them from the offspring of others. Rather, if He willed, He would have created them all together, just as He created Adam from dust. If He willed, He could have made some of them from the offspring of others. However, He does not cause anyone to die until the death of all occurs at one time. So the earth would be too narrow for them, and their livelihoods and earnings would be too narrow for them, and some of them would be harmed by others. But His wisdom and power required that He create them from…” One soul, then He multiplies them to the utmost multitude, and scatters them throughout the earth, and makes them generations upon generations, and nations upon nations, until the term expires and the creation is emptied, as He, the Blessed and Exalted, has decreed, and as He has counted them and counted them. Then He will establish the Resurrection and pay every worker his due when the term has reached his written term. For this reason, the Most High said: Who responds to the distressed when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you successors upon the earth? Is there a deity with God? That is, is He able to do that, or is there a deity with God who is worshipped? And it is known that God is the One Who alone can do that, with no partner or associate? Little do you remember. That is, how little do they remember of what guides them to the truth and directs them to the straight path.
27:63: God the Almighty says: Who guides you through the darkness of the land and sea? That is, through what He created of celestial and earthly signs, as He the Almighty said: And signs and by the stars they are guided. And He the Almighty said: And it is He who made for you the stars that you may be guided by them through the darkness of the land and sea. The verse: And who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? That is, before the clouds in which there is rain with which God helps His eternally barren and despairing servants. Is there a god with God? Exalted is God above what they associate with Him.
27:64: That is, He is the One who, by His power and authority, begins creation and then repeats it, as God Almighty said in another verse: “Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who initiates and repeats.” And God Almighty said: And it is He who initiates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. “And who provides for you from the sky and the earth?” That is, by what comes down from the rain of the sky and what grows from the blessings of the earth, as God Almighty said: And the sky full of paths and the earth full of cracks. And God Almighty said: He knows what goes into the earth and what comes out of it and what comes down from the sky and what ascends therein. So He, Blessed and Exalted be He, sends down blessed water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings forth from it various types of crops, fruits, flowers, and other colors. “Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding.” For this reason, God Almighty said: Is there a god with God? That is, He did this. And according to the other statement after this, Say, ‘Produce your proof,’ for the truth of what you claim of worshipping other gods, if you should be truthful. In this, it is known that they have no argument or proof, as God Almighty said: “And whoever invokes with God another deity for which he has no proof - then his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.”
27:65: God the Almighty commands His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to teach all creation that no one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God. His statement, except God is an interrupted exception, meaning that no one knows that except God, the Almighty, the Majestic, for He is the One who is unique in that, with no partner or associate, as God the Almighty says: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him (al-An'am 2:17). And He the Almighty says: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain (al-An'am 2:18) to the end of the Surah. And there are many verses on this subject. And God the Almighty says: And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected (al-An'am 2:18) meaning that the creatures dwelling in the heavens and the earth do not perceive the time of the Hour, as God the Almighty says: "It is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly" (al-An'am 2:18). Meaning, its knowledge is heavy upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn al-Ja`d told us, Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: Whoever claims that he knows - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - what will happen tomorrow has greatly slandered God, because God Almighty says: “Say: No one in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except God.” Qatada said: God only made these stars for three reasons: He made them an adornment for the heavens, He made them a means of guidance, and He made them missiles for the devils. So whoever deals with them other than that has spoken according to his own opinion, missed his chance, wasted his share, and assumed something of which he has no knowledge. Indeed, ignorant people have invented divination from these stars. Whoever marries under such and such a star will have such and such, whoever travels under such and such a star will have such and such, and whoever is born under such and such a star will have such and such. By my life, there is no star but that red and black, short and tall, handsome and ugly people are born under it. This star, this beast and this bird do not know anything of the unseen. God has decreed that no one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim verbatim. It is a noble, solid and authentic statement. And His statement: “Rather, their knowledge will reach them in the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it.” That is, their knowledge has ended and they are unable to know its time. Others read, Rather, their knowledge will reach them, that is, their knowledge will be equal in that, as in the Sahih of Muslim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel when he asked him about the time of the Hour: The one being asked about it does not know more than the one asking. That is, the knowledge of the one being asked and the one asking are equal in their inability to reach that. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Rather, their knowledge will reach them in the Hereafter, that is, it is absent. Qatada said, Rather, their knowledge will reach them in the Hereafter, meaning because of their ignorance of their Lord, meaning that they will not have knowledge of the Hereafter. This is one statement. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Rather, their knowledge will reach them in the Hereafter, when knowledge will be of no benefit. Ata’ al-Khurasani and al-Suddi said this, that their knowledge will only be reached and completed on the Day of Resurrection when it will not benefit them, as God, the Most High, said, I will hear of them and see them on the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers, that Day, are in manifest error. And He said, Sufyan, on the authority of Amr bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to recite: Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them. He said: Their knowledge in this world has vanished when they see the Hereafter. And the Almighty’s statement: Rather, they are in doubt about it refers back to the genus, and what is meant are the disbelievers, as the Almighty said: “And they will be presented before your Lord in rows. You have certainly come to Us as We created you the first time. Rather, you claimed that We would not make for you an appointment.” That is, the disbelievers among you. And likewise He said here: Rather, they are in doubt about it, that is, they doubt its existence and occurrence. Rather, they are blind to it, that is, in blindness and great ignorance about its matter and its situation.

27:67: God Almighty says, informing them about the polytheists who denied the resurrection, that they ruled out the return of bodies after they had become bones, ashes, and dust. Then He said: This has already been promised to us, us and our fathers before, meaning we and our fathers have continued to hear about this, but we do not see its reality or its occurrence. And their saying, This is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning what is this promise of the return of bodies? It is nothing but legends of the ancients, meaning that a people took it from those before them from books that some people receive from others, and it has no reality. God Almighty said, answering them about what they thought of disbelief and the lack of al-Qiyamah 75:Say, O Muhammad, to these people, Travel through the land and see what was the end of the criminals, meaning those who denied the messengers and what they brought them of the matter of the resurrection and other things, how God’s punishment, torment, and chastisement befell them, and God saved from among them His noble messengers and those who followed them from the believers. This indicates the truth and soundness of what the messengers brought. Then God Almighty said, consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And peace be upon him, And do not grieve over them, meaning those who deny what you have brought, and do not feel sorry for them or grieve over them, and do not be in distress over what they are plotting, meaning your plotting and rejecting what you have brought, for God will support and aid you and make your religion prevail over those who oppose and defy it in the East and the West.

27:71: God the Almighty says, informing about the polytheists in their question about the Day of Resurrection and their rejection of its occurrence: And they say, ‘When is this promise, if you should be truthful?’ God the Almighty says, answering them: Say, O Muhammad, Perhaps there will be followed for you some of that which you are hastening. Ibn Abbas said: That it will be brought near or that some of that which you are hastening will be brought near to you. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said. This is what is meant by God the Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘When is it?’ Say, ‘Perhaps it will be near.’ God the Almighty also said: They urge you to hasten the punishment, while Hell will encompass the disbelievers. The lam was included in His saying: followed for you because it included the meaning of hastened for you, as Mujahid said in a narration from him: Perhaps there will be followed for you means hastened for you. Then God the Most High said: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to mankind, meaning in His bestowal of His blessings upon them despite their injustice to themselves, and despite that, they do not thank Him for that except a few of them. And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare, meaning He knows the innermost thoughts and secrets as He knows the outward appearances. Whether among you conceals his speech or declares it publicly, “He knows the secret and what is more hidden,” Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Then God the Most High informed us that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth and that He knows the unseen and the witnessed, which is what is hidden from His servants and what they witness. So God the Most High said: And there is nothing hidden, Ibn Abbas said: meaning there is nothing in the heaven and the earth but is in a clear register. This is like His saying: “Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a register. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.”

Ibn Abbas said: That it will be brought near or that some of that which you are hastening will be brought near to you. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said. This is what is meant by God the Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘When is it?’ Say, ‘Perhaps it will be near.’ God the Almighty also said: They urge you to hasten the punishment, while Hell will encompass the disbelievers. The lam was included in His saying: followed for you because it included the meaning of hastened for you, as Mujahid said in a narration from him: Perhaps there will be followed for you means hastened for you. Then God the Most High said: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to mankind, meaning in His bestowal of His blessings upon them despite their injustice to themselves, and despite that, they do not thank Him for that except a few of them. And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare, meaning He knows the innermost thoughts and secrets as He knows the outward appearances. Whether among you conceals his speech or declares it publicly, “He knows the secret and what is more hidden,” Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Then God the Most High informed us that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth and that He knows the unseen and the witnessed, which is what is hidden from His servants and what they witness. So God the Most High said: And there is nothing hidden, Ibn Abbas said: meaning there is nothing in the heaven and the earth but is in a clear register. This is like His saying: “Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a register. Indeed, that, for God, is easy.”
27:76: The Almighty says, informing about His Noble Book and what it contains of guidance, clarification and criterion, that He narrates to the Children of Israel, who are the bearers of the Torah and the Gospel, Most of that over which they differ, such as their differences and variations concerning Jesus. The Jews fabricated and the Christians went to extremes, so the Qur’an came with the middle, true and just statement, that he is a servant of God’s servants, His noble prophets and messengers, upon him be the best of prayers and peace, as the Almighty said: That is Jesus, the son of Mary, the statement of truth about which they are in dispute, and His statement, And indeed, it is guidance and mercy to the believers, meaning guidance for the hearts of those who believe in him and mercy for them in actions. Then the Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them meaning on the Day of Resurrection by His judgment, and He is the Exalted in Might meaning in His vengeance, the Knowing of the actions and words of His servants, so rely upon God meaning in all your affairs and convey the message of your Lord, Indeed, you are upon the clear truth meaning you are upon the clear truth even if those who oppose you, for whom misery has been decreed, oppose you and the word of your Lord has come true upon them that they will not believe even if every sign comes to them. For this reason the Almighty said: Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear meaning you cannot make them hear anything that benefits them. Likewise, these people have a covering over their hearts and in their ears is the deafness of disbelief. For this reason the Almighty said: “And you cannot make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs, departing. And you cannot guide the blind from their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims” meaning only the One who hears and sees, hearing and sight that are beneficial in the heart and insight, who submits to God and to what came from Him through the tongues of the Messengers, peace be upon them.

27:82: This beast will emerge at the end of time when people become corrupt and abandon God's commands and change the true religion. God will bring forth for them a beast from the earth. It was said: From Mecca, and it was also said: From elsewhere, as will be detailed later, God willing. It will speak to the people about that. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him said: It will speak to them, meaning it will address them directly. Ata' Al-Khurasani said: It will speak to them and say to them: The people did not believe in Our signs. This was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Jarir preferred it. There is a flaw in this statement that is not hidden, and God knows best. Ibn Abbas said in a narration: It will wound them, and another narration from him said: No, it will do this and that, and it is a good statement and there is no contradiction, and God knows best. There are many hadiths and narrations that mention the Beast, so let us mention what is easy from them, and God is the source of help. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us from Furat, from Abu Tufail, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked out at us from a room while we were discussing the Hour and said: “The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the Beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the west, one in the east, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, driving or gathering people, spending the night with them where they spend the night, and resting with them where they rest.” This is how Muslim and the Sunni scholars narrated it through various chains of narration from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Abu Tufail Amir ibn Wathilah, from Hudhayfah, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Abdul-Aziz ibn Rafi’, from Abu Tufail, with a chain of transmission ending with him. And God knows best. Another way Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said on the authority of Talha bin Amr and Jarir bin Hazim. As for Talha, he said: Abdullah bin Ubaid God bin Umair al-Laithi told me that Abu al-Tayyib told him on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid al-Ghifari Abu Sariha. As for Jarir, he said: On the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid on the authority of a man from the family of Abdullah bin Masoud. Talha’s hadith is more complete and better. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the beast and said: “It will have three emergences in the course of time: It will emerge once from the farthest desert, but its mention will not enter the village - meaning Mecca - then it will lie dormant for a long time. Then it will emerge another time later, and its mention will be high among the people of the desert, but its mention will enter the village - meaning Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then while the people were in the greatest and most honored of mosques before God, the Sacred Mosque, they were startled by it approaching between the Corner and the Station, shaking the dust off its head. The people turned away from it in groups and together, and a group of believers remained and they knew that they had not defeated God. It began with them and shone their faces until it became like a shining star. It turned around on the earth, and no seeker could catch it, and no fugitive could escape from it. Even if a man seeks refuge from it by praying, it will come to him from behind and say: O so-and-so, now you are praying. So he turns to it and it marks him on his face. Then it will go off and the people will share in the money and accompany each other in…” The cities, the believer is known from the disbeliever, to the point that the believer says: O disbeliever, give me my right, and to the point that the disbeliever says: O believer, give me my right.” And Ibn Jarir narrated it through two chains of narration on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid, with a chain of narration ending with him, and God knows best. And he narrated it on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman with a chain of narration ending with the Prophet, and that it was during the time of Jesus, son of Mary, while he was circumambulating the House, but its chain of narration is not authentic. Another hadith Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: I memorized from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a hadith that I have not forgotten since. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from the west, and the emergence of the beast among the people at noon. Whichever of them comes before the other, the other will follow it soon.” Another hadith Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-Ala’ bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Ya’qub, the freedman of Al-Harqa, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hasten to do good deeds before six things happen: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the Antichrist, the beast, the fate of one of you, and the affairs of the masses.” He is the only one to narrate it. He also narrated from the hadith of Qatada, from Al-Hasan, from Ziyad bin Rabah, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Hasten to do good deeds before six things happen: the Antichrist, the smoke, the beast, the rising of the sun from the west, the affairs of the masses, and the fate of one of you.” Another hadith Ibn Majah said: Harmalah ibn Yahya told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith and Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib on the authority of Sinan ibn Sa’d on the authority of Anas ibn Malik on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Hasten to do good deeds before six things happen: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the Antichrist, the affliction of one of you, and the general affairs of the people.” He is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Aws ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Beast of the Earth will emerge, with the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon, peace be upon them both, and it will crush the nose of the unbeliever with the staff and will polish the face of the believer with the ring, until the people will gather at a table and the believer will be known from the unbeliever.” Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Bahz, Affan, and Yazid ibn Harun, all three of them on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on his authority. He said: “It will crush the nose of the unbeliever with the ring and will polish the face of the believer with the staff, until the people at a table will gather and he will say: This one is a believer, and he will say: This one is a unbeliever.” Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu’addib, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on his authority. Another hadith Ibn Majah said: Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Numailah told us, Khalid ibn Ubayd told us, Abdullah ibn Buraydah told us on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took me to a place in the desert near Mecca. There was dry land surrounded by sand, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The beast will emerge from this place. Then it cooled down a handspan. Ibn Buraydah said: So I performed Hajj after that, after several years, and he showed us his staff, and behold, it was like this and this with my staff. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatadah that Ibn Abbas said: It is a furry beast with four legs from some of the valleys of Tihamah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyyah, who said: Abdullah said: The Beast will emerge from a crack in Safa, like a horse running for three days, a third of which it will not emerge. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, who said: Abdullah bin Amr was asked about the Beast, and he said: The Beast will emerge from under a rock in Jihad. By God, if I were with them, or if I wished, I could reach the rock from under which the Beast will emerge with my staff. It was said: What will you do, Abdullah bin Amr? He said: You will face the east and cry out a cry that will penetrate it, then you will face the Levant and cry out a cry that will penetrate it, then you will face the west and cry out a cry that will penetrate it, then you will leave Mecca and arrive in Usfan in the morning. It was said: Then what? He said: I do not know. Abdullah bin Umar said: The Beast will emerge on the night of Jumu’ah. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and in its chain of transmission is Ibn Al-Baylaman. On the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: He narrated from the words of Ezra, peace be upon him, that he said: “And from beneath Sodom will emerge a beast that will speak to the people, everyone who hears it. It will give birth before the full term, fresh water will return to being brackish, friends will become hostile, wisdom will be burned, knowledge will be taken away, and the land below it will speak. At that time, people will hope for what they will not attain, and they will tire themselves out for what they will not attain, and they will work for what they will not eat.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Saleh, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Muawiyah ibn Saleh told me, on the authority of Abu Maryam, that he heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: The beast will have animals of every color, and between its horns is a farsakh for the rider. Ibn Abbas said: It is like a huge spear. On the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “It is a beast with feathers, down, and hooves, but it has no tail and a beard. It will come out like a fine horse three times, and a third of it will not come out.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr that he described the Beast and said: Its head is the head of a bull, its eye is the eye of a pig, its ear is the ear of an elephant, its horn is the horn of a deer, its neck is the neck of an ostrich, its chest is the chest of a lion, its color is the color of a leopard, its flank is the flank of a cat, its tail is the tail of a ram, and its legs are the legs of a camel. Between every two joints are twelve cubits. With it will come out the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon. Not a believer will remain but that a white dot will be made on his face by the staff of Moses, and that dot will spread until his face turns white. Not a disbeliever will remain but that a black dot will be made on his face by the ring of Solomon. That black dot will spread until his face turns black, to the point that people trade in the markets: How much is this, O believer, or how much is that, O disbeliever? Even when the people of a household sit at their table they can tell who is a believer from who is a disbeliever. Then the Beast will say to them: O so-and-so, be of good tidings, you are among the people of Paradise, and O so-and-so, you are among the people of Hell. This is what God Almighty said: And when the word comes to pass against them, We will produce for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, because people were not certain of Our signs.
27:83: God the Almighty says, informing us about the Day of Resurrection and the gathering of the wrongdoers among those who denied the signs of God and His Messengers before God the Almighty, to ask them about what they did in this world, as a rebuke, rebuke, belittling and humiliating. God the Almighty says: And the Day We shall gather from every nation a company meaning from every people and generation a company of those who denied Our signs as God the Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their mates and He the Almighty said: And when souls are paired and His statement: And they will be driven in ranks Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: They will be pushed. Qatada said: A distribution, the first of them will be returned to the last of them. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: They will be driven until, when they come and stand before God, the Almighty, in the place of questioning, He will say, ‘Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge? What were you doing?’ That is, they will be questioned about their beliefs and deeds! So since they were not among the people of happiness and were as God said about them: He neither believed nor prayed, but lied and turned away, then the proof was established against them, and they had no excuse to offer, as God, the Almighty, said: This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will permission be given to them to make excuses, and likewise He said here: And the word will fall upon them for what they did, so they will not speak, that is, they will be stunned and they will have no answer because they were in darkness for themselves in this world, and they have been returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed from whom nothing is hidden. Then the Almighty said, drawing attention to His perfect power, great authority, and exalted status, which requires obedience to Him, submission to His commands, and belief in His prophets in what they brought of the truth from which there is no escape. The Almighty said: Do they not see that We have made the night for them to rest therein? That is, in the darkness of the night, so that their movements may calm down and their breathing may be still, and they may rest from the fatigue of their day. And the day is seeing. That is, luminous and bright. Because of that, they manage their livelihood, earnings, travel, trade, and other matters that they need. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.

Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Ubaydullah ibn Muadh al-Anbari told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Salim, I heard Ya’qub ibn Asim ibn Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi, I heard Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with him, and a man came to him and said: What is this hadith that you narrate, that the Hour will come at such and such a time? He said: Glory be to God, or there is no god but God, or a word like that. I intended never to tell anyone anything. I only said that you will see in a little while a great matter that will destroy the House, and it will happen and happen. Then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Antichrist will emerge among my nation and will remain for forty – I do not know whether it will be forty days, forty months, or forty years – then God will send Jesus, son of Mary, who looks like Urwah ibn Mas`ud, and he will seek him out and destroy him. Then the people will remain for seven years with no enmity between two people. Then God will send a cold wind from the direction of Ash-Sham, and no one will remain on the face of the earth in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of goodness or faith except that it will take him, so that if one of you were to enter the heart of a mountain, it would enter upon him until it took him.” He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They will say: What do you command us to do?” He will command them to worship idols, and they will be in that house of provision and good living. He said: Then he will be stunned and the people will be stunned. Then God will send - or he said God will send down - rain like dew - or he said: shade, Naaman the doubter, and the bodies of the people will grow from it. Then it will be blown again, and they will be standing, looking. Then it will be said: O people, come to your Lord and stop them, for they will be questioned. Then it will be said: Bring out the party of the Fire. It will be said: How many? It is said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. He said: That is the Day when children will turn gray, and that is the Day when the shin will be uncovered. And His statement: Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will bend his neck and raise his head. The layt is the side of the neck, meaning he will bend his neck to hear it from the sky well. This is the blast of terror, then after that is the blast of the stunned, which is death, then after that is the blast of the rising of the Lord of the Worlds, which is the resurrection from the graves of all creatures. For this reason, the Most High said: And all will come to Him humbled. It was read with the extension and without it on the basis of the verb, and all have one meaning, and humbled means humbled and obedient, no one will fail to obey His command, as the Most High said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise. And the Most High said: Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge. And in the hadith of the Trumpet, it is that at the third blast, God will command the souls to be placed in a hole in the Trumpet, then Israfil will blow into it after the bodies have grown in their graves and places. So when the Trumpet is blown, the souls will fly away. The souls of the believers will glow with light, and the souls of the unbelievers will be in darkness. Then God the Almighty will say: By My glory and majesty, every soul will return to its body. So the souls will return to their bodies and stir within them as poison stirs within a stung person. Then they will rise, shaking the dirt from their graves. God the Almighty will say: The Day they emerge from the graves quickly, as if they were, toward an idol, hastening. God the Almighty said: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the clouds pass. That is, you will see them as if they are fixed and remaining as they were, but they will pass as the clouds pass, that is, they will move from their places, as God the Almighty said: The Day the sky will sway with a sway * And the mountains will move with a movement. You will see therein no crookedness or unevenness.’” God the Almighty said: And the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth appearing as a plain. Who perfected all things, that is, He perfected all that He created, and He deposited in it the wisdom that He deposited. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do, that is, He is All-Knowing of what His servants do, of good and evil, and He will reward them for it with the most complete reward. Then God the Almighty explained the state of the happy and the miserable on that Day, saying: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. Qatada said: With sincerity. Zayn al-Abidin said: It is ‘there is no god but God.’ And God the Almighty explained in another place that he will have ten times the like of it. And they will be safe from the terror of that Day, just as He said in the other verse: The greatest terror will not grieve them. And God the Almighty said: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? And God the Almighty said: And they will be in the chambers secure. For this reason God the Almighty said: Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? Zayn al-Abidin said: It is ‘there is no god but God.’ And God the Almighty explained in another place that he will have ten times the like of it. And they will be safe from the terror of that Day, just as He said in the other verse: The greatest terror will not grieve them. And God the Almighty said: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? And God the Almighty said: And they will be in the chambers secure. And His statement: And whoever brings evil, their faces will be thrown into the Fire, meaning whoever meets God having done wrong and has no good deeds, or his bad deeds will outweigh his good deeds, each according to his situation. For this reason God the Almighty said: Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, Anas bin Malik, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Abu Wa’il, Abu Saleh, Muhammad bin Ka’b, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Zuhri, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Zaid said regarding His statement: And whoever brings evil, meaning polytheism.
27:91: God the Almighty says, informing His Messenger and commanding him to say: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred, and to Him belongs all things. As God the Almighty said: Say, ‘O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship other than God, but I worship God, who will take your souls.’ And adding Lordship to the city is to honor it and take care of it, as God the Almighty said: So let them worship the Lord of this House, * Who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. And His statement, Who has made it sacred, means the One who made it sacred by law and decree because of His making it sacred, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “Indeed, God made this city sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns should not be cut, its game should not be scared away, and its lost property should not be picked up except by one who recognizes it, and its estranged property should not be secluded.” The hadith in full. It has been proven in the Sahihs, Hassans and Musnads through the chains of transmission of a group that provides certainty, as is explained in its place in the Book of Rulings, and praise and thanks be to God. The Almighty’s saying: And to Him belongs all things is a general statement in conjunction with a specific statement, meaning He is the Lord of this city and the Lord and King of everything. There is no god but Him. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, meaning the sincere monotheists who submit to His command and obey Him. And His statement: And that I recite the Qur’an means that I convey it to the people, as in the statement of the Most High: This is what We recite to you, of the verses and the wise remembrance and as in His statement: We recite to you, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh in truth 3:11, meaning I am a conveyor and a warner. “So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever goes astray - say, ‘I am only one of the warners’” meaning that I have an example like the messengers who warned their people, and carried out what they were required to do in delivering the message to them, and were freed from their responsibility and the accountability of their nations to God Almighty, as in His statement: Your burden is only to convey [the message], and upon Us is the account 3:11, and He said: You are only a warner, and God is Disposer of affairs 3:11. “And say, ‘Praise be to God. He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them’” meaning, praise be to God, who does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him and the warning has been directed to Him. For this reason, the Most High said: He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them 3:11, as in His statement: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. And the Almighty said: And your Lord is not unaware of what you do, meaning, He is a Witness over all things. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was reported on the authority of Abu Omar al-Hawdi, Hafs ibn Omar, who said: Abu Umayya ibn Ya’la al-Thaqafi told us, who said: Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id told us, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, let none of you be deceived by God, for if God were unaware of anything, He would have overlooked the mosquito, the mustard seed, and the atom. He also said: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, who said: Nasr ibn Ali told us, who said: My father told me, Khalid ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: If God were unaware of anything, He would have overlooked the traces of the feet of the son of Adam that the winds erase. It was reported on the authority of Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, that he used to recite these two couplets, either for himself or for someone else: If you are ever alone, do not say I am alone, but say I am being watched. Do not think that God is unaware for a moment, nor that what is hidden from Him is hidden. The last interpretation of Surat An-Naml, praise and thanks be to God.
